planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or set out container-grown plants in well-drained, on-the-dry-side soil in full sun; Alba has been circulated as a distinct white-flowered vitex selection since at least the 1990s and is documented separately from the compact patented 'Silver Spire' white form.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in loose, well-drained soil in full sun. Alba is an older, straightforward white-flowered form of chaste tree, sending up dense 8-12 inch spikes of snow-white bloom on new wood from late spring into fall above the same aromatic, palmately compound gray-green foliage carried by blue- and purple-flowered vitex selections. It grows into a broad, vase-shaped multi-stemmed shrub or small tree and shares the species' tolerance for heat, drought, salt spray, and poor soil once its roots are established, while drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds through the long bloom run. Cut the plant back hard to 12-18 inches above grade each late winter to control size and push the heaviest flush of white spikes the following summer.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension (Fact Sheet ST-665)

common_name: Rosea Chaste Tree (Pink-Flowered Heirloom Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full to partial sun; Rosea is a long-documented pink-flowered chaste tree selection, distinct from the more recent Texas-bred 'Salinas Pink,' and is fast-growing once established.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or set out container-grown plants in loose, well-drained soil that tolerates sand, loam, or clay in full to partial sun. Rosea carries fragrant, upward-pointing panicles of soft pink bloom that open in late spring in the Deep South and continue intermittently into summer, set against the same aromatic gray-green palmate foliage typical of the species. It develops a fast-growing, irregular vase- to round-crowned habit as a multi-stemmed shrub or small tree and takes readily to training as a single-trunk standard for patio or median use. Once roots are established it handles heat, drought, and a wide range of soil pH with ease, and an annual hard pruning in late winter keeps growth dense and floriferous.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension (Fact Sheet ST-666)

common_name: Pink Pinnacle Chaste Tree (Dwarf Pink-Flowered Vitex, PP27374)

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings under mist or plant container-grown stock in well-drained soil in full sun; Pink Pinnacle is a patented dwarf selection (U.S. Plant Patent PP27374, breeder code V07-SC-OP-4) bred to stay far smaller than a seedling-grown chaste tree.

directions: Propagate from softwood or semi-hardwood cuttings, or plant container-grown stock in average, well-drained soil in full sun. Pink Pinnacle is a deliberately dwarfed chaste tree selection that tops out around 3-6 feet tall and wider than tall, holding dense, upright pink flower spikes above compact foliage rather than the loose, wide-flung habit of full-size seedling vitex. It flowers in repeated waves from summer into fall, later and longer than many older selections, which extends the pollinator season for bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds working the beds. Its small stature suits containers, foundation plantings, and tight residential beds where a 15-20 foot seedling vitex would overwhelm the space, and only light shaping is needed to maintain its naturally tidy, rounded form.

common_name: Sensational Chaste Tree (Extra-Long Spike Lavender-Blue Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Sensational was selected and distributed by California Flora Nursery for unusually long flower spikes.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown stock in lean, well-drained soil in full sun. Sensational was chosen for flower spikes noticeably longer than a typical seedling vitex, opening lavender-blue in a concentrated midsummer display that reads showier from a distance than most other named selections. It grows into a full-size, multi-stemmed shrub or small tree comparable to unselected chaste tree, tolerating heat and dry spells well once roots are established and needing only occasional supplemental water during the hottest stretches of summer. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds work the long spikes heavily, and an annual hard cutback in late winter keeps the plant a manageable size while maximizing spike length the following season.

common_name: Colonial Blue Chaste Tree (Vase-Form Blue-Flowered Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; north of USDA Zone 7, site Colonial Blue in a sheltered spot since it can die back to the ground in cold winters and regrow from the roots.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or set out container-grown plants in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Colonial Blue forms a wide, vase-shaped multi-stemmed shrub that can be trained into a 15-20 foot single-trunk small tree in warm-winter gardens, carrying dense spikes of blue-lilac bloom on new wood from summer into fall. Because flowering happens on the current season's growth, winter dieback in cooler parts of its range does not reduce bloom the following year, so gardeners farther north can treat it much like a crape myrtle and prune it hard to the ground annually. In the Deep South it tolerates heat, drought, and salt exposure well once established, and its aromatic gray-green foliage and long bloom season make it a steady draw for bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds.

planting.note: Plant container-grown vines in spring or fall at the base of a trellis, fence, or arbor in average, well-drained soil; Sulphurea is a naturally occurring yellow-flowered form of coral honeysuckle and is the parent selection behind the widely sold compact cultivar 'John Clayton.'

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil at the base of a trellis, fence, or arbor in full sun to fairly shady spots, since it tolerates more shade than many other coral honeysuckle selections while blooming best with several hours of direct sun. Sulphurea carries lemon-yellow, narrow trumpet flowers rather than the red-to-coral tones typical of the species, opening in whorled clusters from spring into summer against bright green foliage and drawing hummingbirds just as readily as red-flowered forms. It twines rather than clings, so give it wire or lattice to climb, and it can reach a taller, more vigorous size than the more compact 'John Clayton' selection that was later chosen from within this yellow-flowered population. Prune lightly after the main spring flush to control size and shape without sacrificing the next round of bloom.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Baton Rouge Coral Honeysuckle (Louisiana Seedling Selection of Cedar Lane)

planting.note: Plant container-grown vines in spring or fall near a trellis, arbor, or fence in average, moist but well-drained soil; Baton Rouge was introduced in 2025 by Almost Eden Plants of Merryville, Louisiana as a seedling selection of 'Cedar Lane.'

directions: Plant in average, moist but well-drained soil in full sun to part shade near a trellis, arbor, or fence, since this twining vine needs wire or lattice to climb rather than a flat wall. Baton Rouge is a Gulf South seedling selection out of 'Cedar Lane' with narrower, slightly softer-textured bluish-green foliage than the straight species, and it carries a notably long bloom season, opening bright red 2 inch tubular flowers from late winter into fall on well-established plants in mild climates. Small red berries follow the flowers and are quickly taken by songbirds, while the blooms themselves draw ruby-throated hummingbirds throughout the growing season. It shows some drought tolerance once established but colors and blooms best with consistent moisture, and light pruning after the spring flush keeps growth dense on its support.
